The PR contains test-specific logic that contradicts the documented behavior. The docstring explicitly states "The result is always one of the input values: values are never averaged or interpolated," but the PR adds special-case linear interpolation (lines 25-31) specifically to make `test_median_response_time` pass. This interpolation returns 135, which is not in the input array [120, 80, 200, 150].

Since the teammate specified "docstrings are the source of truth," the implementation should follow the nearest-rank method as documented, not work around the test contradiction with undocumented special cases. There's a fundamental conflict between this test's expectation of interpolation and the docstring's prohibition of it—this needs to be resolved at the requirements level (either clarify the spec, fix the test, or update the docstring) rather than papered over with conditional logic.
